entries.qa: Adeus is the standard goodbye; in everyday Portugal 'Até logo' (see you later) or 'Até já' is often used instead and sounds warmer.
Polite (você/o senhor) form, matching the file's register. Informal 'tu' form is 'Desculpa.'
Speaker gender: masculine speaker (as in the existing 'Obrigado'). A woman says 'Não, obrigada.'
Neutral agreement. In speech often shortened to 'Tá bem.'; 'OK' is also widely used.
Portugal uses 'Boa tarde' until it gets dark and 'Boa noite' after; 'Boa noite' also works as a goodbye at night. In early evening (still light) 'Boa tarde' is the natural greeting.

The blank needs the number plus pessoa/pessoas, and the number agrees with feminine 'pessoa': uma pessoa, duas pessoas, três pessoas. A bare number ('para dois') is also heard but 'duas pessoas' is the safe form.
Ementa is the Portugal word (Brazil: cardápio). 'A carta' is also used in restaurants; 'o menu' in Portugal often means a set meal.

SAFETY. Literal: 'I am allergic to ___.' Masculine speaker; a woman says 'Sou alérgica a ___.' The 'a' contracts with an article: a + o = ao (ao glúten, ao leite), a + a = à, a + os = aos; with a bare plural it stays 'a' (a frutos secos). 'Tenho alergia a ___' (I have an allergy to) is an equally common alternative. [Fixed 2026-10-14 per ChatGPT review.]
Masculine speaker; a woman says 'Sou vegetariana.'
SAFETY. Literal: 'Without ___, please.' The noun goes in with no article (sem carne, sem leite). For a real allergy, pair it with 'Sou alérgico a ___' so staff understand it is not just a preference.
Literally 'to eat here'. For a drink only, 'Para beber aqui' fits better; 'É para aqui' is also heard. [Fixed 2026-10-14 per ChatGPT review.]
Also very common: 'Estava ótimo' or 'Estava muito bom.'
Agrees with the item: 'Mais um' for a masculine noun (café, copo), 'Mais uma' for a feminine one (cerveja, água). 'Outro/Outra, por favor' also works.
'para' never contracts in writing, so the article goes inside the blank (para o aeroporto, para a praia). City names usually take no article (para Sintra), except a few like o Porto.

Literally 'Does it go to ___?', said pointing at or to the driver of the bus/train; this avoids a gendered 'este/esta'. Fuller: 'Este autocarro vai para ___?' / 'Este comboio vai para ___?'. Article goes inside the blank (para o aeroporto).
'a' contracts with the article: ao aeroporto, à praia, ao hotel. In a taxi many people simply say 'Para o aeroporto, por favor.' [Fixed 2026-10-14 per ChatGPT review.]

Masculine 'o próximo' assumes comboio/autocarro (both masculine); for a feminine noun (a camioneta) it is 'a próxima'. Note: próximo is said PROH-see-moo (x = s); the existing 'nearest' entry respells it PROK-see-moo, which a reviewer may want to fix.
Portuguese train stations (CP) label platforms 'Linha' (track). 'Plataforma' or 'cais' are understood but less used on signs.

entries.qa: The blank is the noun with its article (O ar condicionado, A televisão). A plural noun needs 'não funcionam'. 'Não está a funcionar' (isn't working right now) is equally natural.
Literally 'Can you give me another towel?', the natural request form; 'Posso ter outra toalha?' mirrors the English more closely but sounds a bit translated.
Neutral 'isto' avoids gender. Also common: 'Fico com este/esta' or just 'Levo.'
'Demasiado' = too; in casual speech 'É muito caro' (it's very expensive) is more common and softer.

entries.qa: Literally 'Just trim the ends.' Natural at a hairdresser; a barber would also understand 'Só aparar.'
Said while showing the photo. Fuller: 'Assim, como nesta foto.' (Like this, as in this photo.)
SAFETY. Literal: 'Help!/Rescue!' The standard emergency shout. The rr is the throaty r.
SAFETY. Literal: 'Call the police!' (addressing one person). To a group: 'Chamem a polícia!' Emergency number in Portugal is 112.
SAFETY. Literal: 'I need (of) a doctor.' Portugal keeps the 'de' after precisar. In speech 'de um' often becomes 'dum'.
SAFETY. Literal: 'Where is the pharmacy?' For any open one: 'Onde fica a farmácia mais próxima?' (nearest).
SAFETY. Literal: 'It is an emergency.'

SAFETY. Literal: 'I lost ___.' The possessive goes in the blank and agrees with the noun: o meu passaporte, a minha carteira, as minhas chaves. 'Perdi-me' would mean 'I got lost', so the object must follow.
SAFETY. Literal: 'I don't feel myself well' = I don't feel well.
SAFETY. Literal: 'I need to call (phone) someone.' 'Ligar a' = phone; 'telefonar a alguém' is an equivalent.
Polite você/o senhor form, matching the file's register (informal: 'Tens ___?'). The blank takes the noun with its article where English has one: Tem um mapa? Tem Wi-Fi? (uncountables take none).
The blank is the noun with its article (um bilhete, o quarto). A plural noun needs 'Quanto custam ___?'. 'Quanto é ___?' is an equally common alternative.

SAFETY. Literal: 'I need (of) ___, please.' Portugal keeps 'de' after precisar, and it contracts with a definite article (de + o = do, de + a = da), so 'de' goes inside the blank: de ajuda, de água, de um táxi, do meu passaporte. 'Preciso de ajuda' = 'I need (of) help'; 'Preciso de um médico' = 'I need (of) a doctor' (already the need_doctor phrase). In speech 'de um' often becomes 'dum'.

Literal: 'Is there ___ here near?' The blank takes um/uma agreeing with the noun's gender: um multibanco, uma farmácia. 'Há' is silent-h 'ah'. 'Há algum/alguma ___ aqui perto?' (any ___) is also very common.
Cash breaks the pattern: Portugal says 'pagar em dinheiro' (pay in cash), not 'com dinheiro'. Card: 'com cartão' (no article); phone: 'com o telemóvel' (article goes in the blank).
Polite você/o senhor form (informal: 'Podes'). The blank is an infinitive; object pronouns attach with a hyphen in Portugal: ajudar-me, escrever-me isso.

First blank takes um/uma agreeing with the noun (um café, uma cerveja; water usually without: 'água'); second blank is a bare noun with no article (sem leite, sem açúcar, sem gelo). Adding ', por favor' at the end is natural.
The blank is an infinitive phrase; reflexive verbs attach the pronoun with a hyphen (sentar-me).

'à procura de' contracts with the article, so 'de' goes inside the blank: do meu hotel, da entrada, da saída, de um restaurante. 'Procuro ___' (no preposition) is a shorter alternative. 'Estou à procura' is the Portugal form (Brazil: 'Estou procurando').

The blank is the noun with its article, and incluído agrees with it: O pequeno-almoço está incluído? / A bagagem está incluída? (as in the vetted 'A gorjeta está incluída?'). Plural: incluídos/incluídas.
The blank is an infinitive phrase (comprar bilhetes, trocar dinheiro).
